notes.summary: Average covers the mean of a set of values, weighted averages, and how an average changes when items are added, removed, replaced or corrected. SSC CGL usually asks 1-2 questions on it: cricket innings, replacing a person, overlapping groups, ages of a family, and average speed.
keyPoints: Average = Sum ÷ Number of items, and Sum = Average × Number. Most questions are solved by working with sums, not averages.

For consecutive numbers or any arithmetic progression, average = (first + last) ÷ 2 = the middle term. The average of the first n natural numbers = (n + 1)/2, of the first n even numbers = n + 1, and of the first n odd numbers = n.
Weighted average = (n1 × a1 + n2 × a2) ÷ (n1 + n2). Example: 30 boys averaging 60 and 20 girls averaging 70 give 3,200 ÷ 50 = 64.
Replacement: new person − old person = number of items × change in average. Example: in a group of 8, if the average rises by 2.5 kg, the newcomer is 20 kg heavier than the person replaced.
New innings: if the (n + 1)th score raises the average by d, then new average = score − n × d. Example: 85 in the 17th innings raising the average by 3 gives 85 − 48 = 37.
If every value is multiplied by k and then c is added, the average is also multiplied by k and then increased by c.
Average speed over equal distances at x and y = 2xy/(x + y). For three equal distances at x, y and z = 3xyz/(xy + yz + zx).
Overlapping groups: the common middle item = (sum of first part + sum of last part) − total sum.
A wrongly copied value shifts the average by (correct − wrong) ÷ n.
traps: Taking the simple average of two group averages when the groups are of different sizes.
Averaging speeds directly: 40 and 60 km/h over equal distances give 48 km/h, not 50.
In age questions, forgetting that every member ages by the same number of years, or counting a member who was not yet born.
In replacement and new-entry questions, forgetting to multiply the change in average by the number of items.
notes.examTip: Use the deviation method: assume a convenient value and average the deviations. For 47, 52, 49 and 56, take 50: (−3 + 2 − 1 + 6)/4 = 1, so the average is 51.

questions.text: What is the average of the first 50 natural numbers?
questions.explanation:
The average of the first n natural numbers is (n + 1)/2.
= (50 + 1)/2 = 25.5.
Check: sum = 50 × 51/2 = 1,275, and 1,275/50 = 25.5.

questions.text: The average of 7 consecutive natural numbers is 20. What is the largest of these numbers?
questions.explanation:
For consecutive numbers, the average is the middle (4th) number, which is 20.
The numbers are 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23.
The largest number is 23.

questions.text: In a class, the average marks of 30 boys is 60 and the average marks of 20 girls is 70. What is the average marks of the whole class?
questions.explanation:
Total marks = 30 × 60 + 20 × 70 = 1,800 + 1,400 = 3,200.
Total students = 50.
Average = 3,200/50 = 64.
Note: 65 is wrong because the two groups are of different sizes.

questions.text: The average of 5 numbers is 30. If each number is multiplied by 3 and then 5 is added to each, what is the new average?
questions.explanation:
Any operation applied to every value is applied to the average in the same way.
New average = 30 × 3 + 5 = 95.

questions.text: The average of four consecutive even numbers is 27. What is the largest of these numbers?
questions.explanation:
Let the numbers be x, x + 2, x + 4 and x + 6. Their average is x + 3 = 27, so x = 24.
The numbers are 24, 26, 28 and 30.
The largest number is 30.

questions.text: The average of 6 numbers is 8. If one number is removed, the average of the remaining numbers becomes 7. What is the number that was removed?
questions.explanation:
Sum of 6 numbers = 6 × 8 = 48.
Sum of the remaining 5 = 5 × 7 = 35.
Removed number = 48 − 35 = 13.

questions.text: The average weight of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person comes in place of one of them who weighs 65 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
questions.explanation:
Total increase in weight = 8 × 2.5 = 20 kg.
The new person weighs 20 kg more than the person replaced.
New person = 65 + 20 = 85 kg.

questions.text: A batsman scores 85 runs in his 17th innings and thereby increases his average by 3 runs. What is his average after the 17th innings?
questions.explanation:
Let the average after 16 innings be x. Then 16x + 85 = 17(x + 3).
16x + 85 = 17x + 51, so x = 34.
New average = 34 + 3 = 37.
Shortcut: new average = 85 − 16 × 3 = 37.

questions.text: The average of 11 results is 50. The average of the first 6 results is 49 and the average of the last 6 results is 52. What is the 6th result?
questions.explanation:
The 6th result is counted in both groups.
Sum of the first 6 + sum of the last 6 = 6 × 49 + 6 × 52 = 294 + 312 = 606.
Sum of all 11 = 11 × 50 = 550.
6th result = 606 − 550 = 56.

questions.text: The average age of a family of 5 members is 24 years. If the youngest member is 8 years old, what was the average age of the family at the time of the birth of the youngest member?
questions.explanation:
Present total age = 5 × 24 = 120 years.
The other 4 members' total now = 120 − 8 = 112 years.
8 years ago their total = 112 − 4 × 8 = 80 years, and the family had only 4 members.
Average = 80/4 = 20 years.

questions.text: A car travels from town A to town B at 40 km/h and returns from B to A at 60 km/h. What is its average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation:
The distances are equal, so average speed = 2xy/(x + y).
= 2 × 40 × 60/(40 + 60) = 4,800/100 = 48 km/h.
Note: 50 km/h is the simple average and is wrong here.

questions.text: The average of 50 numbers was found to be 38. Later it was discovered that the number 82 had been wrongly copied as 28. What is the correct average?
questions.explanation:
The sum was short by 82 − 28 = 54.
The average increases by 54/50 = 1.08.
Correct average = 38 + 1.08 = 39.08.

questions.text: The average weight of A, B and C is 45 kg. The average weight of A and B is 40 kg and that of B and C is 43 kg. What is the weight of B?

The average salary of all the workers in a workshop is ₹8,000. The average salary of 7 technicians is ₹12,000 and the average salary of the rest is ₹6,000. What is the total number of workers in the workshop?
questions.explanation:
Let the total number of workers be n.
7 × 12,000 + (n − 7) × 6,000 = 8,000n.
84,000 + 6,000n − 42,000 = 8,000n, so 2,000n = 42,000 and n = 21.
Shortcut (alligation): technicians : others = (8,000 − 6,000) : (12,000 − 8,000) = 1 : 2, so there are 7 technicians and 14 others, 21 in total.

questions.text: The average age of a husband and wife was 23 years at the time of their marriage. After 5 years, they have a one-year-old child. What is the average age of the family now?
questions.explanation:
At marriage, total age = 2 × 23 = 46 years.
After 5 years, the couple's total = 46 + 2 × 5 = 56 years.
Adding the child: 56 + 1 = 57 years for 3 members.
Average = 57/3 = 19 years.

questions.text: A man's average monthly expenditure is ₹4,000 for the first 3 months of a year, ₹4,500 for the next 4 months and ₹5,200 for the remaining 5 months. If he saves ₹16,000 during the whole year, what is his average monthly income?
A cricketer whose bowling average is 12.4 runs per wicket takes 5 wickets for 26 runs in a match and thereby decreases his average by 0.4. How many wickets had he taken before this match?
questions.explanation:
Let n be the wickets taken before the match. Runs conceded = 12.4n.
After the match: (12.4n + 26)/(n + 5) = 12.0.
12.4n + 26 = 12n + 60, so 0.4n = 34 and n = 85.
Check: (1,054 + 26)/90 = 1,080/90 = 12. He had taken 85 wickets.

questions.text: The captain of an 11-member cricket team is 26 years old and the wicket-keeper is 3 years older. If their ages are excluded, the average age of the remaining players is 1 year less than the average age of the whole team. What is the average age of the team?
questions.explanation:
Let the team's average be A. The captain and wicket-keeper together are 26 + 29 = 55 years.
11A − 55 = 9(A − 1).
11A − 55 = 9A − 9, so 2A = 46 and A = 23.
Check: (253 − 55)/9 = 198/9 = 22, which is 1 less. The average is 23 years.

questions.text: A person covers three equal distances at speeds of 10 km/h, 20 km/h and 60 km/h respectively. What is his average speed for the whole journey?
questions.explanation:
Let each distance be 60 km (the LCM of 10, 20 and 60).
Time = 60/10 + 60/20 + 60/60 = 6 + 3 + 1 = 10 hours.
Average speed = total distance/total time = 180/10 = 18 km/h.
Formula: 3xyz/(xy + yz + zx) = 36,000/2,000 = 18 km/h.

questions.text: Of three numbers, the first is twice the second and the second is twice the third. If the average of the reciprocals of the three numbers is 7/72, what is the largest number?
questions.explanation:
Let the third number be x. Then the second is 2x and the first is 4x.
Sum of reciprocals = 1/(4x) + 1/(2x) + 1/x = (1 + 2 + 4)/(4x) = 7/(4x).
Average = 7/(12x) = 7/72, so x = 6.
Largest number = 4x = 24.
